Two trades wrapped up, two carried forward

Drew, here is your October 2026.

Your month mixed two positions carried in from August with two new ones: a KO covered call and a SHOP custom position from before the month, then an INTC long call opened on Oct 7 and F shares bought on Oct 22. The new trades were bought for a debit rather than sold for premium. KO was assigned on Oct 14, you closed INTC on Oct 27 with about 3 weeks still left before expiration, and SHOP and F were carried into next month.

AT A GLANCE
- 2 trades: new trades you started
- 1 time: times you rolled a trade to a new strike or expiration
- none: share of your rolls done for a credit
- about 6 weeks: how far out the expiration usually was when you opened an options trade

GETTING IN
- You usually opened options trades expiring about 6 weeks out.
- You usually paid a debit of $143 per contract when you opened a trade.
- Implied volatility was usually average compared with its past year when you opened a trade.

MANAGING

- None of your rolls were done for a credit.

GETTING OUT
- You usually kept a trade for about 6 weeks.
- When you closed an options trade, it was usually still 12 days from expiration.
- You closed 1 trade that ended with a loss before expiration.

WHAT STOOD OUT
Your new trades were bought, not sold. The INTC long call opened on Oct 7 with its expiration about 6 weeks out, for a debit of $715. The F shares followed on Oct 22 for $3,124. Neither new position collected premium; both put money in up front.

The two losing trades ended in different ways. The KO covered call ran its course and was assigned on Oct 14 after about 2 months, a loss of $601. The INTC long call you closed yourself on Oct 27, before its expiration day, for a loss of $251.

SHOP was the one position you adjusted. On Oct 26 you rolled the SHOP position down to a lower strike and out to a later expiration, and the roll was not done for a credit. Rather than closing it, you kept SHOP open into next month alongside the F shares.

HOW IT TURNED OUT

Of the 2 trades that ended, 0 ended with a gain and 2 with a loss.
Fees and commissions: at least $8.74.

WHAT CHANGED
